solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Giant pig carrying dog around

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the whole assembly back to front
the pig word holds the dog word within it, as if bearing it

parts.note: a hog is a pig
to dog someone is to tail them, follow closely

explanation.surface: A huge pig has a dog on its back as it trots about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' is the verb, to follow. 'carrying' puts the dog word after the H to make HTAILOG, and 'around' turns that whole string back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: The Philistine champion slain by David is the proverbial giant of the Bible.

clue.text: Leave spouse in Bow and settle equitably

parts.note: to go is to leave
'my old Dutch' is Cockney for one's wife; Bow is in the East End of London, home of Cockneys

explanation.surface: Someone walks out on their partner in an East London district and splits things fairly.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is a district of London's East End, so 'in Bow' signals Cockney speech, where 'Dutch' (from duchess) means one's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to pay half each, sharing a bill evenly between the diners.

clue.text: Sound tip for music writer

indicators.note: sound tells us the entry is said like the word meaning tip

parts.note: to list is to tip or lean over, as a ship does

explanation.surface: Sound advice for someone who writes about music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective (sound tip = good advice) but signals the homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was the Hungarian composer and pianist of the Romantic era.

clue.text: Finding energy in a can, dined at home

indicators.note: in places the energy letter within the words for a can

parts.note: a tin is a can
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone eats in, getting a boost from canned food.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb: to eat a meal in one's own house rather than out.

clue.text: Man United having to manage wisely

definitions.meaning: a man united with a woman in marriage, her spouse
as a verb, to use resources thriftily, conserve them

explanation.surface: Manchester United must run the club with care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man United' is the usual name for Manchester United football club; here it is a married man.
explanation.definitionFit: A spouse is a man joined in wedlock; the verb sense means to economise with resources.

clue.text: Old soldier fired in anticipation

indicators.note: in puts the fired word inside the anticipation word

parts.note: hope is hopeful anticipation
lit means set alight, fired

explanation.surface: A veteran shot his gun in expectation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fired' looks like gunfire but is LIT, set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavily armed infantryman of ancient Greece was a soldier from long ago.

clue.text: Buoy, made with clay, but hard on top

indicators.note: on top says the hard letter shifts to the head of this down entry

parts.note: earthen pots are made of baked clay
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A float made of clay, but with a hard shell on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buoy' reads as a float but is the verb, to cheer up. In EARTHEN the H moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To buoy someone up is to encourage and lift their spirits.

clue.text: Air ace unsettled patriot holding Bible

indicators.note: holding means the shuffled patriot surrounds the Bible letters
unsettled means the letters of patriot are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: A flying ace, a restless patriot, carrying scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' is a tune, not the sky, so the ace is a singer. 'unsettled' gives PAROTTI, and 'holding' places the Bible letters just after its P.
explanation.definitionFit: Luciano Pavarotti was a star tenor, a virtuoso of the operatic aria.

clue.text: Big limo or convertible in massive jam

indicators.note: convertible means the letters can be converted into another form

explanation.surface: A big limousine or soft-top caught in a huge traffic jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convertible' looks like a car, fitting the limo, but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An entanglement or complicated, embarrassing situation is a figurative mess or fix.

clue.text: Refusal to receive Liberal is picked up in letter

indicators.note: picked up, in a down clue, means the assembly is lifted and read upwards
to receive means the refusal word takes in the following letters

parts.note: nope is a casual refusal

explanation.surface: A refusal to accept a political party member is collected in a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' looks like a homophone signal, but in a down entry it means lifted: 'to receive' makes NOLISPE, which reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifth character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Heartburn Pepys said should be treated

indicators.note: treated means worked on, so the letters are processed into a new order

explanation.surface: The diarist Samuel Pepys reports that his heartburn needs medical care.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigestion, of which heartburn is a common symptom.

clue.text: Against introducing one live percussion instrument

indicators.note: introducing means the following letters are brought into the against abbreviation

parts.note: VS is short for versus, against
I is the Roman numeral one
to be is to live, exist

explanation.surface: A drummer opposes bringing in a single live instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for vibraphone, a tuned metal-barred percussion instrument.

clue.text: Bottom fan in ship, American, initially cut out

indicators.note: in says the American letter is put into the ship's name
out says that first letter is taken out of the ship's name

parts.note: the Titanic is the famous ship

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of cut

explanation.surface: A fan of someone's backside travels on a ship, an American one, with something cut away.
explanation.walkthrough: In TITANIC, the C (start of 'cut') goes out and A goes in. In Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, the fairy queen falls for Bottom the weaver.
explanation.definitionFit: The bewitched fairy queen dotes on the weaver who wears an ass's head, so she is his admirer.

clue.text: Speaker's expression, crude perhaps, bringing disorder

indicators.note: Speaker's means the expression word as spoken gives the first syllable

parts.note: a term is a word or expression
crude is one kind of oil, oil unrefined

explanation.surface: A speaker's coarse language causes chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crude' looks like coarse language but is crude oil.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of great confusion and upheaval is a synonym for disorder.

clue.text: Here plant growth may be seen in graph done wrongly

definitions.text: Here plant growth may be seen

indicators.note: wrongly means the letters are done in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A chart of plant growth has been badly drawn.
explanation.walkthrough: A hop garden is a field where hops for brewing are grown, a feature of Kent in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot where hop vines climb poles and wires, so a place to watch a crop grow.

clue.text: Ceremony requires a severe hairstyle

parts.note: pomp is ceremonial splendour
dour means stern, severe

explanation.surface: A formal occasion calls for a strict hairdo.
explanation.definitionFit: A style with the hair swept up high off the forehead, named after Madame de Pompadour.

clue.text: An Italian city and southern capital

parts.note: Napoli is the Italian name for Naples

explanation.surface: An Italian city that is also a capital of the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'southern capital' reads as one phrase, but S is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The seat of government of the US state of Maryland, home of the Naval Academy.

clue.text: Short story being broadcast, one that grips

indicators.note: short means the story word loses its last letter

parts.note: a tale is a story
a programme being broadcast is on, on air

explanation.surface: A short story on the radio grips the listener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one that grips' suggests a gripping tale, but it is a bird's claw.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird of prey's claw is what seizes and holds its prey.

clue.text: Spirit seen in March and November

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A ghost appears in two months of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March and November' look like months; March is a demonstration.
explanation.definitionFit: An evil supernatural being, a malign spirit.

clue.text: Rod following obese man sent north

indicators.note: sent north, in a down entry, means the pieces read upwards

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
fat means obese
Sid is a man's name

explanation.surface: A stick chasing a fat man who has been packed off north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rod' looks like a man's name joining the scene; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The stick holding unspun wool or flax in hand spinning.

clue.text: Problem for walker on island, needing sign

indicators.note: on means the foot problem comes after the island in this across entry

parts.note: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples
a corn is a painful patch of hard skin on the foot

explanation.surface: A hiker on an island has trouble that calls for a signpost.
explanation.definitionFit: The goat, one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Hint given about one error in French cooking

indicators.note: about means the hint word goes round the other letters

parts.note: a cue is a hint or prompt
I is the Roman numeral one
a sin is an error, wrongdoing

explanation.surface: A tip about a single mistake in French cookery.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is French for kitchen or cookery, a style of preparing food.

clue.text: Young man breaking bread for French champion

indicators.note: breaking means the young man splits the bread word open

parts.note: pain is French for bread
a lad is a young man

explanation.surface: A youngster breaking bread with a French hero.
explanation.definitionFit: One of Charlemagne's twelve knights, hence a heroic champion of a cause.

clue.text: Late shift perhaps in close connection

parts.note: nigh means near, close
a tie is a bond or connection

explanation.surface: Working the night shift brings close colleagues together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late shift' looks like a work rota; a shift is a loose dress, here one worn at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightdress is a loose garment, a kind of shift, for bedtime.

clue.text: Dog that is sent back after biting

indicators.note: after means the reversed letters follow the biting word

parts.note: sharp means biting, keen

indicators.note: sent back means the that-is abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: IE is id est, that is

explanation.surface: A dog is returned after it bit someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrinkled Chinese breed of dog with a blue-black tongue.

clue.text: Base has cargo brought round front

indicators.note: brought round means the cargo word is placed around the base letter

parts.note: lading is a load or cargo, as in bill of lading
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A military base takes in a delivery brought up to the front line.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, foremost, at the head, as in the leading edge.

clue.text: German newspaper article drawn up freely

indicators.note: drawn up, in a down entry, means the letters read upwards

parts.note: Bild is Germany's best-selling tabloid newspaper
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A German newspaper article has been drafted without constraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawn up' looks like drafting a document.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken or performed off the cuff, without preparation or a script.

clue.text: Current understanding serves as example

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
a deal is an arrangement or understanding

explanation.surface: A current agreement sets the standard.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfect model or standard to follow, an exemplar.

clue.text: Books returned in totally tropical paradise

indicators.note: in places the reversed books inside the totally word

parts.note: all means wholly, totally

indicators.note: returned means the books abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Library books are returned in a completely tropical paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring-shaped coral island round a lagoon, the archetypal desert island idyll.

clue.text: Ready to excuse faults in largely boring chap

indicators.note: largely means most of the boring word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: dull means boring
a gent is a chap, a gentleman

explanation.surface: A tedious fellow is readily forgiven his flaws.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenient and tolerant, inclined to overlook others' failings.

clue.text: Predict charge to cover valued metal sources

indicators.note: to cover means the charge word goes around the ores

parts.note: a fee is a charge
ores are rocks mined for metal

explanation.surface: A forecaster's fee is raised to cover the cost of precious metal.
explanation.definitionFit: To see ahead of time, anticipate what will happen.

clue.text: Clouds from high blue area gathered in north-east

indicators.note: gathered in means the shuffled letters are taken inside the north-east pair
high means intoxicated, so the letters of blue reel into a new order

explanation.surface: Clouds from a lofty blue sky have massed in the north-east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' looks like altitude but signals the anagram, making EBUL; 'gathered in' sets EBUL plus A between N and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Interstellar clouds of gas and dust seen in the night sky.
